My research focuses on three interconnected themes. The first is 
local and retrieval-based machine learning for spectroscopy: 
developing methods that exploit the structure of large spectral 
libraries to build adaptive, sample-efficient predictive models 
(including memory-based learning, library search, and evolutionary 
subset selection). The second is chemometrics and applied spectroscopy, 
particularly vis-NIR and MIR applications in soil science and 
agriculture, where I have worked on problems ranging from national-scale 
soil mapping to field-deployable calibration workflows. The third is 
scalable and deployable ML for industrial laboratory applications, 
translating research-grade methods into embedded systems, digital 
products, and analytical services for real-world use.
